newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent a lb weaker on Tuesday based on market orders at 1016 EDT, traders said.
They said Monday's close near the lows could trigger further losses and pegged near-term support at 74.00 cents in December, followed by the contract low of 73.20 cents.
Monday, the benchmark December contract closed 0.58 cent weaker at 75.02 cents a lb. The rest of the board settled 0.25 to 0.57 cent lower.
The October/December spread closed at 0.05 cent compared with 0.15 cent the previous day.
An estimated 9,000 lots changed hands on the day.
Turkey's cotton output is seen at 750,000 tonnes in 1997/98, down from 792,414 tonnes the previous season, Sadi Katircioglu, acting head of Izmar Trade Bourse, said.
He said imports could compensate for lower domestic production and estimated imports at 250,000 tonnes at the end of 1998.

NYCE's weekly spec/hedge report noted that the speculators have moved to a 8.0 percent net short position as of July 25 from a 12.1 percent net short position the week earlier. Market sources said the report is not likely to have any influence over prices today.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture said Monday that 55 percent of the cotton crop is in good to excellent condition compared with 61 percent last week. Dry hot weather in the eastern part of the cotton belt has slowed the development of the crop, industry sources said.
